check_outbound_ip.description: Find out which public IP address your workflows reach the internet from. This is the address to give a service that will only accept requests from an approved list. No API key required.
check_outbound_ip.display_name: Check the IP address we call from
check_outbound_ip.display_str_template: Check the IP address Lodol calls from.
check_outbound_ip.name: check_outbound_ip

ip_address.description: The public IP address the request came from. This is the one to add to an approved list.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

check_request_headers.description: See every header a request from Lodol carries, without setting anything up. Useful when a service is refusing your requests and you need to know what it is actually being handed. To check a header of your own, use Send a test request instead. No API key required.
check_request_headers.name: check_request_headers

header_names.description: Just the names, in alphabetical order, for a step that only needs to check one is there.

headers.description: Every header httpbin received: the ones we send, plus the two the internet adds on the way (Host, and Amazon's trace id).

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

user_agent.description: How Lodol identifies itself. This is the value to give a service that asks you to name your client.

generate_uuid.description: Get a fresh unique ID, different every time. For tagging a run, naming a file, or filling a field that has to be unlike every other one. No API key required.
generate_uuid.name: generate_uuid

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

uuid.description: The ID, as 36 characters with hyphens, e.g. 1b4e28ba-2fa1-11d2-883f-0016d3cca427.

get_sample_document.description: Get a small nested JSON document, the same one every time. Something real-shaped to build the rest of a workflow against while the payload it will really receive does not exist yet. No API key required.
get_sample_document.name: get_sample_document

author.description: Who it says wrote it, lifted to the top.

document.description: The document exactly as httpbin serves it, wrapper and all, so it is a genuinely nested payload to practise reaching into.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

slides.description: Its sections, flattened into one shape so a loop can read them all the same way.

items.description: Its bullet points. Empty for a section that has none.

title.description: The document's title, lifted to the top.

send_test_request.description: Send a request and get the whole thing back: the method, the address, the query values, every header and the body. The step to put in front of a new integration to see exactly what your workflow is sending before you point it at something real. Nothing is stored and nothing is charged. No API key required.
send_test_request.display_str_template: Send a test request to httpbin.
send_test_request.name: send_test_request

parameters.description: How to send it. Every choice comes back the same way, so this is for matching the request your real integration will make.
parameters.name: method

parameters.description: Optional. Names and values to put on the end of the address. They come back under 'query', which is how you check one was filled in from an earlier step.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Optional. Extra headers to send. They come back alongside the ones we always send, which is how you check an authorization or tracking header really left.
parameters.name: headers

parameters.description: Optional. Names and values to send as the JSON body. Numbers, true and false and nested values keep their type, so what comes back is what went out.
parameters.name: body

body.description: The body, read back as JSON with its types intact. Empty when nothing was sent.

body_text.description: The body exactly as it went over the wire. Worth reading when the parsed version surprises you.

called_from_ip.description: The public IP address the request came from.

headers.description: Every header httpbin received: the ones you set, the ones we always send, and the two the internet adds on the way (Host, and Amazon's trace id).

method.description: The method httpbin saw, e.g. POST.

query.description: The query values httpbin read off the address. Always text, because that is all a query string can carry.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The HTTP status httpbin answered with.

url.description: The full address the request arrived at, query values and all.

simulate_response_status.description: Make httpbin answer with the status you choose, so you can build and test the branch that handles it. The step itself always succeeds, even when you ask for a 500: the status comes back as a value to branch on, because a step that failed would leave nowhere to put the branch. No API key required.
simulate_response_status.name: simulate_response_status

parameters.description: The answer httpbin should give. Pick the one your workflow has to survive.
parameters.name: status_code

as_requested.description: True when the status that came back is the one asked for. False means something between here and httpbin answered instead.

category.description: The family it belongs to: Success, Client error, Server error, Redirect or Informational. Branch on this to handle all of a kind at once.

ok.description: True for any status from 200 to 299.

reason.description: What the status means in words, e.g. Not Found.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The status that came back. This is the field to branch on.

simulate_slow_response.description: Make httpbin take its time before answering, so you can see how a workflow behaves against a slow service and whether a timeout is set where you think it is. Up to ten seconds. No API key required.
simulate_slow_response.name: simulate_slow_response

parameters.description: How long httpbin should take before it answers. Between 0 and 10; 3 by default. Fractions are fine.
parameters.name: seconds

requested_seconds.description: The wait that was asked for.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The HTTP status httpbin answered with.

test_basic_auth.description: Send a username and password the way a service expecting them would receive them, and see whether they arrive intact. This is what catches a password with an awkward character in it, or a value that was never filled in from an earlier step. Choose to have them rejected instead and you get the same refusal a real service gives, to build the other branch against. No API key required.
test_basic_auth.name: test_basic_auth

parameters.description: The username to send. Anything but a slash, which httpbin cannot carry.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: The password to send. Nothing is stored, so this is for a test value rather than a real one. Anything but a slash, which httpbin cannot carry.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: Accept the username and password to check that it arrives intact, or reject it to get the same refusal a real service would give, so you can build the branch that handles credentials going bad.
parameters.name: result

authenticated.description: True when they were accepted. This is the field to branch on.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The HTTP status httpbin answered with.

username.description: The username httpbin read back out of the request. Compare it with what you sent to prove it survived the trip.

test_bearer_token.description: Send a token the way an API expecting one would receive it, and get it read back to you. That read-back is the point: it proves the value your workflow built is the value that left the building. Choose to have it rejected instead and you get the same refusal a real API gives, to build the other branch against. No API key required.
test_bearer_token.name: test_bearer_token

parameters.description: The token to send. Nothing is stored, so this is for a test value rather than a real one.
parameters.name: token

parameters.description: Accept the token to check that it arrives intact, or reject it to get the same refusal a real service would give, so you can build the branch that handles credentials going bad.
parameters.name: result

authenticated.description: True when the token was accepted. This is the field to branch on.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The HTTP status httpbin answered with.

token.description: The token httpbin read back out of the request. Empty when it was rejected, because nothing was sent.

test_redirects.description: Send a request through a chain of redirects and see where it ends up. Answers whether Lodol follows redirects at all, and how many deep, which is the usual reason a request that works in a browser does not work in a workflow. No API key required.
test_redirects.name: test_redirects

parameters.description: How long the chain should be. Between 1 and 10; 3 by default.
parameters.name: count

all_followed.description: True when the whole chain was followed. This is the field to branch on.

redirects_followed.description: How many were actually followed, counted from the trip that happened rather than from what was asked for.

redirects_requested.description: How long a chain was asked for.

response_time_ms.description: How long the whole round trip took, in milliseconds. This is the number to compare against a timeout.

status_code.description: The HTTP status httpbin answered with.

description: A dependable place to point a step at while you build a workflow, from httpbin. Send a request and get the whole thing back, so you can see exactly what your workflow sends: the method, the query values, every header and the body. Then force the cases that are hard to arrange for real, and build the branches that handle them: a 500, a 404, a rate limit, a response that takes ten seconds, a chain of redirects, a password or token that gets rejected. It will also tell you which IP address your workflows call from, for a service that keeps an approved list, and hand you a unique ID or a sample document to work against. Nothing is stored and nothing is charged. No account or API key required.
